summary: GFL announced a proposed acquisition of Secure Waste Infrastructure to strengthen its operations in Western Canada. Operational cost and revenue synergies are expected to be material and could represent an incremental 25 to 50 million of opportunity above 25 million of largely SGA cost savings already identified, with Secure's 2026 revenue expected to be 1.5 to 1.6 billion.

headline: GFL Environmental Q1 2026 Earnings Call: Record Margins and Eight Acquisitions Completed
summary: GFL Environmental achieved the highest adjusted EBITDA margin in company history at 29.1%, with pricing growing 7.0% and organic growth of 4.6% in Q1 2026. The company completed eight acquisitions including Frontier Waste Solutions in Texas and announced a proposed acquisition of Secure Waste Infrastructure for Western Canada, with management maintaining target leverage of 3.0-3.5x.

headline: GFL Environmental Completes Eight Acquisitions Including Frontier Waste Solutions; Raises 2026 Guidance
summary: GFL Environmental completed eight acquisitions year-to-date, including Frontier Waste Solutions in Texas. These deals add $425-450M in annualized revenue and further densify GFL's North American network. Proposed SECURE Waste acquisition expected in H2 2026 is described as incremental to current outlook. Net leverage reached 3.6x despite positive operational metrics.

headline: EPA Updates Interim PFAS Destruction and Disposal Guidance
summary: The EPA released updated Interim Guidance on PFAS destruction and disposal published in the Federal Register on April 28, 2026, with public comments due by June 29, 2026. The guidance addresses disposal pathways including landfilling, underground injection, and thermal treatment for PFAS-containing materials.

headline: Queen Sirikit National Convention Center partners with PTTGC to convert used cooking oil into SAF under 'From Kitchen to Creation' initiative
summary: Queen Sirikit National Convention Center launched the 'From Kitchen to Creation' initiative with PTT Global Chemical, collecting used cooking oil from on-site food operations and converting it into SAF, diverting over 68,000 kilograms of food waste and UCO from landfill in 2025.

headline: Loyola University's lab turns used cooking oil into fuel to run buses
summary: Article profiles Loyola University's Searle Biodiesel Lab, which converts used cooking oil collected from Chicago-area restaurants and institutional sources into biodiesel fuel. Green Grease, the local UCO collector, expects to recycle 1 million gallons in 2026.

headline: Weirton Wastewater Plant Upgrade Nears Completion at 96%
summary: Weirton's $38 million wastewater treatment plant upgrade project has reached 96% completion, designed to expand treatment capacity from 4 to 8 MGD. Final payments are expected in late May. The project was triggered by interest from a large manufacturing company looking to locate in the city.

headline: LJP Waste Solutions Acquires United Liquid Waste Recycling
summary: GreyLion Capital-backed LJP Waste Solutions acquires United Liquid Waste Recycling, materially expanding its liquid-waste footprint across Wisconsin and the upper Midwest. First add-on of size for LJP's liquid-waste line and a notable consolidation move outside the named Big-4 platforms.

headline: Q1 2026 Biodiesel Prices and UCO Feedstock Markets Show Seasonal Volatility
summary: Biodiesel prices in Europe reached $1.50/KG in March 2026, with downward pricing movement of 2.0% between December and March. Europe's shift toward waste-based sources like used cooking oil and animal fats created cost pressure, with limited UCO availability supporting higher prices despite increased U.S. exports.

headline: Folly Beach Considers Water and Sewer Fee Increase
summary: Folly Beach City Council considered increasing water and sewer tap and impact fees after a 5-year rate study revealed they were lower than surrounding areas. The ¾-inch water tap and impact fee would increase from $1,375 to $3,500.

headline: Water Sector Groups Press Congress on Funding, PFAS and Affordability During Water Week
summary: Water sector professionals including the Water Environment Federation held meetings with lawmakers during the annual National Water Policy Fly-In in Washington, D.C. Key topics included declining federal water infrastructure investment, PFAS management compliance costs, and the need for reauthorization of Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds.

headline: Driver shortage causing workforce challenges for Roanoke's Solid Waste Management team
summary: The nationwide demand for CDL drivers is creating workforce challenges for Roanoke's Solid Waste Management operations, forcing temporary suspension of recycling services. The city is implementing crew prioritization and developing drop-off sites as interim solutions.

headline: Ara Partners Announces Up to $500 Million Investment in Sedron to Scale Waste Upcycling Technology
summary: Ara Partners, a global PE and infrastructure firm, announced up to $500 million investment in Sedron Technologies to scale its Varcor® technology, which transforms liquid waste streams including biosolids and agricultural manure into reusable water and fertilizer products. Sedron recently announced a strategic partnership with Synagro for a biosolids upcycling facility in Indiantown, Florida, with construction expected to commence spring 2026 and commissioning in 2028.

headline: New Jersey Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Updated Manifest and Violation Penalties
summary: New Jersey enforces strict manifest requirements and civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation per day for missing or fraudulent manifests. Multiple search results from April 2026 confirm continued enforcement of grease trap regulations across municipalities.

headline: Tierra Environmental & Industrial Brings Expanded Waste Solutions to Chicagoland
summary: Tierra Environmental & Industrial, an IEPA-licensed special waste hauler, has expanded operations into the Chicagoland area. The company delivers professional grease trap cleaning, waste management, and industrial cleaning services, with expertise in managing FOG from commercial kitchens and support for regulatory compliance in the Midwest.

headline: 2026 Requirements for Renewable Fuel Producers in State Clean Fuel Programs
summary: California, Oregon, and Washington now require supply-chain attestations for used cooking oil, animal fats, and corn oil feedstocks starting 2026. New Mexico's Clean Fuel Standard begins April 1, 2026. Compliance focuses on feedstock documentation, land-use records, and transparency for UCO and waste grease sources.

headline: Goldman Sachs-backed LES Acquires New Orleans Grease Trap Cleaning
summary: LES continues add-on acquisition strategy under Goldman Sachs ownership, adding a New Orleans-based grease trap cleaning operation to its network.

headline: CARB posts new Frequently Asked Questions for 2025 LCFS amendments
summary: CARB released new FAQs clarifying implementation of 2025 LCFS amendments, which include a 20% cap on virgin soybean and canola oil usage, directing producers toward waste-based UCO and grease feedstocks for biodiesel and renewable diesel production.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Makes New Orleans Acquisition
summary: LES acquired New Orleans Grease Trap Cleaning (NOL), a grease trap and used cooking oil cleaning services provider based in New Orleans. The acquisition expands LES' network of nonhazardous wastewater collection facilities. LES has executed a series of strategic acquisitions including Grease Masters in December 2025.

headline: DeKalb County FOG Program Reduces SSO Causation from 57% to 52% via Enhanced Inspections
summary: In DeKalb County, Georgia, FOG was responsible for 57% of SSOs in 2014; thanks to efforts of the county's FOG inspectors, this figure dropped to under 52%. All FSEs in DeKalb County must have a Grease Control Device with 30-90 day cleaning cycle using licensed hauler.

headline: GFL Environmental Proposes Acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure
summary: GFL Environmental announced a proposed acquisition of SECURE Waste Infrastructure to strengthen its operations in Western Canada. SECURE's revenue in 2026 is expected to be 1.5 to 1.6 billion.

headline: Meridian Waste acquires Waste Knot, LLC
summary: Meridian Waste Virginia acquired Waste Knot, LLC effective April 1, 2026, strengthening its footprint in the Richmond market. The transaction increases route density and drives volume to the company's vertically integrated MRF and landfill assets.

headline: Clean Harbors Issues PFAS Disposal and Treatment Guidance Standards
summary: Clean Harbors released its PFAS management framework in early April, providing an end-to-end cost-effective solution for PFAS in multiple forms and concentrations. The company generated more than $120 million in PFAS-related revenue in 2025, with a pipeline growing about 20% and now seeing growth in the 25% to 35% range for 2026.

headline: EPA Finalizes Historic 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard with Record-High Volumes
summary: The EPA finalized the 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard with all-time-high renewable volume obligations of 25.82 billion RINs in 2026 and 25.98 billion RINs in 2027, including 70% reallocation of small refinery exemptions. Biomass-based diesel nearly doubles to 8.86 billion RINs in 2026, directly supporting renewable diesel and biodiesel producers using waste-based feedstocks like UCO.

headline: U.S. Diesel Prices Spike to $5.40/Gallon Following Middle East Supply Disruptions
source: U.S. Energy Information Administration / Quarterly Update
summary: On March 30, the U.S. average retail diesel price of $5.40/gal was the highest in real terms in over two years, following supply disruptions tied to Middle East military action.

headline: Miller Environmental Group completes acquisitions of Haz-Mat Environmental Services and Canco
summary: Miller Environmental Group, a Coalesce Capital portfolio company, completed acquisitions of Haz-Mat Environmental Services and Canco, expanding its industrial waste treatment and disposal capabilities.

headline: 2026 International Day of Zero Waste Focuses on Food Waste Prevention – Global ESG Momentum Builds
summary: UNEP shifts global narrative on food waste from consumer behavior issue to systems-level ESG priority. Recognition of food loss/waste as central to sustainable consumption, biodiversity, pollution reduction, and climate change. Emphasizes governance structures and public-private partnerships to scale solutions.

headline: Water Infrastructure Grants in 2026: CWSRF, IIJA Programs, and USDA Funding for Clean Water Projects
summary: Federal water infrastructure funding in 2026 totals billions through EPA's Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds, with IIJA authorization running through FY2026. States are actively seeking projects to obligate remaining funds before the authorization window closes.

headline: Wind River Environmental Acquires East Coast Resources
summary: Wind River Environmental acquired East Coast Resources, a Fuquay Varina-based company specializing in grease trap pumping. The deal expands Wind River's footprint in North Carolina and continues its consolidation strategy.

headline: EPA Authorizes Local FOG Ordinances via Clean Water Act NPDES Framework
summary: EPA's Clean Water Act regulations authorize municipalities to require grease interceptors as part of local pretreatment programs, with compliance depending on jurisdiction-specific FOG ordinances. Unpermitted FOG discharge can result in municipal citations with penalties ranging from $500 to $5,000 per violation.

headline: Illinois Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Chicago FOG Program Enforcement Update
summary: Illinois regulations require grease trap cleaning every 90 days minimum with penalties starting at $500 and escalating to $10,000 for repeat violations. The Metropolitan Water Reclamation District (MWRDGC) enforces FOG compliance across Chicago and 128 suburban communities.

headline: Colorado Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Denver and Fort Collins FOG Control Mandates
summary: Colorado Water Quality Control Division oversees FOG pretreatment regulations with local enforcement in Denver, Colorado Springs, Aurora, and Fort Collins. The state mandates 25-33% capacity rules and quarterly to monthly cleaning frequencies.

headline: North Carolina Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — Charlotte Water FlowFree Program Expansion
summary: North Carolina municipalities including Charlotte, Raleigh, Durham, and Greensboro enforce FOG regulations with violations ranging from $250 to $1,000+. Charlotte Water's free FlowFree program allows restaurants to submit maintenance documents directly online.

headline: Massachusetts Grease Trap Regulations 2026 Guide — MWRA and Boston Compliance Requirements
summary: Massachusetts mandates 1,000-gallon minimum capacity and 4-foot depth grease traps. Municipal penalties range from $25–$200 per day. The Board of State Examiners of Plumbers enforces code 310 Mass. Reg. 15.230 specifications.

headline: EPA Announces Final 2026-2027 RFS Volumes with 70% Reallocation of Small Refinery Exemptions
summary: EPA announced final 2026-2027 RFS volumes at the highest levels in program history, with record renewable fuel requirements. The agency reallocated 70% of exempted volumes from 2023-2025, eliminating renewable electricity (eRINs) from the program and deferring a 50% RIN reduction on imported fuels until 2028.

headline: Update on the 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard Biofuels Mandate
summary: Analysis of EPA's final 2026-2027 RFS volumes announcing record-high requirements with biomass-based diesel nearly doubling from 2025 levels. The rule includes projections of 41.9 billion gallons of renewable fuel supply growth over two years.

headline: Georgia Oak Partners Acquires Septic Blue
summary: Private equity sponsor Georgia Oak Partners acquired Septic Blue, a Southeast regional leader in septic tank services operating in Atlanta, Charlotte, and Raleigh metro areas. Source Capital provided debt financing and equity co-investment.

headline: Barrel Energy Inc. (OTC: BRLL) Acquires Renewable Energy Company Happy Traps to Expand Waste-to-Energy Platform
summary: Barrel Energy acquired Happy Traps, a Portland, Maine waste-to-energy and environmental services company, which has 200+ recurring commercial clients and >3,500 grease trap cleanings with customer retention above 95%, positioning Barrel Energy to expand its grease-management services into the $8+ billion U.S. market.

headline: Waste Hauling Insurance: Why Recycling & Garbage Companies Are Getting Hit at Renewal
summary: Waste and recycling haulers face increased exposure and liability challenges securing adequate insurance coverage. The sector is experiencing difficult renewal conditions as companies navigate complex risk profiles across diverse operations.

headline: Wind River Environmental Acquires J&M Transfer, Inc.
summary: Wind River continues aggressive expansion, acquiring J&M Transfer to extend its liquid waste transfer capabilities.

headline: Miami-Dade Grease Trap Compliance for Restaurants 2026 — Federal Consent Decree Enforcement Remains Strict
summary: Miami-Dade enforces FOG compliance under a federal consent decree with 90-day cleaning maximums and 99% efficiency requirements. A February 2026 County Commission resolution signals potential future relief, though current regulations remain fully enforceable.

headline: CDL rule affecting non-citizens taking effect despite waste hauler concerns
summary: A federal CDL eligibility rule restricting non-domiciled drivers took effect March 16, 2026, immediately affecting up to 20% of Waste Pro's drivers in Southwest Florida. The regulation impacts asylum seekers, refugees, and DACA recipients previously eligible for commercial licenses, exacerbating existing driver shortages.

headline: LCFS 2024 Amendments: Tightened CI Targets and Expanded Verification Framework
summary: California's 2024 LCFS amendments, effective July 1, 2025, significantly tightened credit supply and expanded producer obligations. The 2025 reporting year required GREET 4.0 model use, and 2026 brings expanded feedstock and land-use documentation for renewable fuels from waste oils including UCO.

headline: Junk Removal Business Insurance Cost (2026 Rates)
summary: Broad waste/junk removal insurance survey noting that disposal fees and regional regulations significantly affect both operations and risk exposure for hauling businesses.

headline: FMCSA CDL Rule Restricting Non-Domiciled Drivers Takes Effect; Waste Haulers Face 20% Driver Impact
summary: FMCSA final rule affecting CDL eligibility for nearly 200,000 drivers took effect, restricting certain non-domiciled drivers including asylum seekers and refugees from holding CDLs. Waste Pro reports the rule change would affect up to 20% of its drivers in Southwest Florida, delaying service and making it hard to replace qualified drivers.

headline: Quatra Secures 15-Year Used Cooking Oil Supply Agreement with TotalEnergies
source: Coherent Market Insights / Used Cooking Oil Market Report
summary: Quatra signed a 15-year agreement to supply TotalEnergies with 60,000 tons of European used cooking oil annually from 2026, to be processed into biodiesel and sustainable aviation fuel.

headline: CDL Immigration Rule Impact: Federal Rules Bar Asylum Seekers from Commercial Driving
summary: Federal rules implemented in March 2026 now bar asylum seekers, refugees, and DACA recipients from obtaining or renewing CDLs, with an estimated 200,000 active CDL holders—roughly 5% of all commercial drivers—directly affected. Texas is the epicenter of the driver shortage impact due to its high freight volume and disproportionate immigrant driver population.

headline: The Future of FOG Compliance: What's Coming in 2027 and Beyond
summary: EPA's draft 2026 guidance clarifies that chemical or biological FOG treatment does not constitute legal 'removal' under Clean Water Act standards. Water Environment Federation laboratory studies show these products can increase downstream FOG deposits by 30-40%, prompting regulatory bodies and municipalities to enforce mechanical removal as the only defensible compliance strategy.

headline: EPA Draft Guidance: Chemical/Biological FOG Treatment Does Not Constitute 'Removal'
summary: The EPA's draft 2026 guidance clarifies that chemical or biological FOG treatment does not qualify as 'removal' under Clean Water Act standards. Water Environment Federation research shows biological additives can increase downstream FOG deposits by 30-40%, pushing regulatory focus toward mechanical removal and IoT-enabled grease interceptor monitoring.

headline: Seekye Capital Acquires SES Mid Atlantic, Advantage Septic and Joiner Micro Laboratories
summary: Private equity firm Seekye Capital announced its inaugural acquisition creating a comprehensive wastewater and environmental services platform. The deal brings together soil/environmental consulting, septic services, and environmental lab capabilities.

headline: Black Box Intelligence: 9% of Full-Service Restaurants at Risk of Closure in 2026
summary: Black Box Intelligence data shows 9% of full-service restaurants are at risk of shuttering, while only 4% of limited-service units could close this year. For the 3% of Full-Service restaurants experiencing sales drop exceeding 50%, the question for 2026 isn't if they will close, but when.

headline: Fats, Oils, and Grease Stormwater Pollution
summary: Municipal FOG pollution prevention page updated with current regulatory and environmental compliance information. Notes EPA estimate that 47% of sewer blockages are due to grease from restaurants and industrial sources.

headline: Raleigh, NC FOG Program Updates – Municipal ESG Compliance & Infrastructure Oversight
source: City of Raleigh, NC Official Website
summary: City of Raleigh updates FOG stormwater pollution program guidance (last updated Feb 3, 2026). Emphasizes EPA estimate that 47% of sewer blockages are FOG-related; reinforces municipal FOG permitting and compliance framework as part of broader ESG infrastructure goals.

headline: Insurance for Waste & Recycle Haulers: Protecting Your Business and Operations
summary: Article discusses rising insurance costs for waste and recycling haulers in 2026, noting increased exposure and liability challenges. Liquid waste haulers are called out as requiring special pollution liability endorsements and additional coverage.

headline: Used Cooking Oil Market Valuation Reaches $8.47B in 2026; Set to Grow to $13.86B by 2033
source: Coherent Market Insights / UCO Market Report
summary: Used Cooking Oil Market valuation is estimated to reach USD 8.47 Bn in 2026 and is anticipated to grow to USD 13.86 Bn by 2033 with steady CAGR of 7.3%. The food service segment is anticipated to account for 46.9% of the UCO market in 2026, with North America leading the global market at 45.2% share.

headline: Food Waste Laws & Regulations in the USA in 2026: ESG Compliance Requirements Tighten
summary: Comprehensive review of 2026 food waste regulations across U.S. states, with emphasis on organics diversion, FOG management compliance, and ESG reporting requirements. California SB 1383 now requires 97% of jurisdictions to operate integrated organics programs; emphasis on waste-to-energy and alternative treatment technologies.

headline: PFAS Behavior During Water and Wastewater Treatment
summary: The Global Waste Management Symposium (GWMS) session on 'PFAS Behavior During Water and Wastewater Treatment' explored mechanics of contaminant management during treatment processes.

headline: Papa John's Announces 200 Restaurant Closures in 2026; 300 Total by End of 2027
summary: Papa John's announced in a February 26 earnings call that it plans to close about 200 restaurants in 2026 as part of broader effort to shut down 300 underperforming locations by end of 2027. Most franchised locations slated for closure are over a decade old, with average unit volume under $600,000 and typically negative four-wall income.

headline: ESG in the Food Industry: Enhancing Transparency and Accountability
summary: Discusses ESG frameworks and standards required in food sector operations, covering environmental footprint, supply-chain sustainability, worker welfare, and food safety. Addresses how food waste reduction fits into ESG compliance strategies for food companies.

headline: Fats, Oils, and Grease (FOG) Management in the Restaurant Sector: A Study of Guadalajara
summary: Peer-reviewed research on FOG management examining collection systems, restaurant practices, and grease trap waste characterization. Emphasizes circular economy approaches and FOG valorization through energy recovery pathways to address environmental sustainability.

headline: Austin Wastewater Plant Expansion Costs to Increase $600M
summary: City officials considered a $600 million (66%) cost increase to the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion project. The total project cost rose to $1.5 billion due to rising costs of goods and services, site constraints, and other factors. The project aims to increase capacity to 100 MGD by 2032.

headline: What to Know About the Section 45Z PTC Proposed Regulations
summary: Treasury and IRS issue proposed regulations for Section 45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit covering transportation fuels including biodiesel from used cooking oil. Credit amounts up to $1/gallon for qualifying facilities through 2027, with heightened scrutiny on imported UCO feedstock sourcing.

headline: Average Waste Management CDL Driver Salary Reaches $29.71/Hour; Shortage Persists
source: ZipRecruiter / Hazardous Waste Driver Salary Data
summary: As of May 1, 2026, the average hourly pay for hazardous waste driver in the United States is $28.59; most workers earn between $24.28 and $30.05 per hour depending on experience, location, and employer.

headline: The Water and Wastewater Equipment, Treatment and Transport (WWETT) Show 2026 Celebrates Industry-Leading Innovations and Solutions
summary: The WWETT Show 2026 successfully concluded its Indianapolis edition (Feb 16-19) with a 6% attendance increase over 2025. The expo floor showcased cutting-edge products and solutions including water filtration, robotics, portable systems, and AI-powered dash cams addressing industry's evolving needs.

headline: Depot Connect International Sells Industrial and Rail Services Business to Clean Harbors
summary: Clean Harbors completed an acquisition of industrial and rail services from Depot Connect International as referenced in Q1 2026 earnings announcements, supporting the company's strategic growth in industrial services.

headline: WWETT Show 2026 Concludes with Record Attendance and Industry Innovation
summary: The WWETT Show 2026 successfully concluded February 16-19 at the Indiana Convention Center with a 6% increase in attendance from the 2025 edition. The expo floor featured cutting-edge products including water filtration systems, robotics, portable systems, and AI-powered dash cams, with education tracks covering pipe lining, sewer relining, and portable sanitation.

headline: Valorization of used cooking oil: challenges, current developments, life cycle assessment and future prospects
summary: Academic review examining global UCO recycling landscape with annual production of 41-67 million tons. Explores waste-to-value pathways including biodiesel, bioasphalt, and biopolymers; notes only 10-20% of food service UCO is currently collected for recycling.

headline: City of Stanton RFP for Environmental Services for NPDES and FOG Programs
summary: The City of Stanton is requesting proposals from qualified consultants to provide services for National Pollutant Elimination Systems (NPDES) and Fats Oils & Grease (FOG) programs with question deadline March 11, 2026.

headline: Liquid Environmental Solutions Acquires Commercial Pumping Services
summary: Liquid Environmental Solutions has acquired Commercial Pumping Services, a leading provider of grease trap and used cooking oil collection services. Based in St. Charles County, MO and founded in 2000, Commercial Pumping Services will be added to LES' extensive network of non-hazardous wastewater collection facilities.

headline: Sustainable transformation of waste cooking oil: A global review of valorization pathways and future directions
summary: Comprehensive review of WCO conversion technologies (2019-2025), highlighting biodiesel production efficiencies of 87-96% and emerging applications in bio-jet fuels, bio-asphalt, and biopolymers. Identifies need for next-generation catalysts and machine learning optimization.

headline: [Date unverified] Regulatory Update: Iowa EPA FCG Program Developments and Clean Water Standards
summary: Unpermitted FOG discharge can result in municipal citations with penalties ranging from $500 to $5,000 per violation, mandatory equipment installation, increased inspection frequency, and cost recovery if discharge causes infrastructure damage. The Clean Water Act authorizes civil penalties up to $59,973 per violation per day for unpermitted discharges.

headline: [Date unverified] WEFTEC 2026 Conference Scheduled for New Orleans
summary: WEFTEC 2026, the Water Environment Federation's 99th Annual Technical Exhibition and Conference, is scheduled for September 26-30 at the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center in New Orleans. The event will feature water quality education, networking opportunities, and cutting-edge solutions for wastewater and environmental professionals.

headline: [Date unverified] Kitchen Carbon Offsets: What §45Z Makes Your Grease Worth – Federal Tax Credits Transform Used Cooking Oil Finance
summary: Article analyzes how the Inflation Reduction Act's §45Z Clean Fuel Production Credit creates federal tax incentives (up to $0.70/gal) for low-carbon biodiesel from recycled cooking oil. California alone could unlock ~$32M in annual credit value; the three-year credit window runs through 2027 before sunsetting.

headline: [Date unverified] Portable Toilet & Liquid Waste Software
summary: CRO's liquid waste management software for septic, porta potty, and grease trap services with real-time asset tracking, FOG regulation compliance, smart reporting tools, and customizable service frequencies. Supports both owner-operators and multinational enterprises.
